Surah al-Tur (Makkiyya, and its verses are forty-nine)

﴿By the Mount (al-Tur)﴾, i.e., the mountain upon which Allah spoke to Musa (Moses).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 3:

﴿In a scroll unrolled﴾ i.e., the Torah or the Qur'an

**Wal-Bayt al-Ma'mur** (the Frequented House): it is in the third, sixth or seventh heaven, directly opposite the Ka'bah. Seventy thousand angels visit it every day for circumambulation and prayer; they never return to it again.
﴿And the raised canopy﴾, i.e., the sky.
﴿And by the sea that is filled (al-masjur)﴾, i.e., the one that is full (al-mamlu').
﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾ — it will descend upon the one who deserves it.

﴿ما لَهُ مِن دافِع﴾ عَنْهُ

Translation:

﴿It has no repeller﴾ (of it)

**﴿Yawm﴾** is a *ma'mul* (the element governed by a word, here the object of *wāqi'*), and it is governed by *wāqi'*. **﴿Tamūru as-samā'u mawrā﴾** means: the sky will sway and revolve, moving and spinning.
And the mountains will move, moving (away) — becoming scattered dust, and that is on the Day of Resurrection.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 52, verse 11:

﴿Woe﴾ meaning severity of punishment; ﴿on that Day to those who deny﴾, that is, those who deny the Messengers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 12:

﴿Those who are in vain discourse﴾ [engaged in falsehood] ﴿playing﴾, i.e., they occupy themselves with their disbelief.

On the Day they will be driven ﴿yudaʽʽūna﴾ into the Fire of Hell with violent shoving, ﴿daʽʽan﴾. This is a *badal* (a grammatical substitution, or apposition, which restates the preceding noun) for "the Day" in ﴿the Day the sky will sway violently﴾. They are pushed with force, and it will be said to them as a rebuke (*tabkītan*): ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 15:

﴿Is this magic?﴾ That is, this punishment you are seeing, as you used to say about the revelation, "This is magic."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 52, verse 16:

﴿Burn therein (ižlawhā); then whether you bear it with patience or do not bear it with patience (fa-iṣbirū aw lā taṣbirū), it is all the same for you (sawāʾun ʿalaykum)﴾ — meaning: whether you endure it patiently (ʿalayhā) or do not endure it patiently, your patience and your impatience and lamentation (jazaʿakum) [are equal]; ﴿it is all the same for you﴾ because your patience will not benefit you. ﴿You are only being repaid for what you used to do﴾, i.e., its recompense (jazāʾahu).

﴿Enjoying﴾ (taking delight) ﴿in what﴾ (the *mā* is a *maṣdariyyah*, a verbal-noun particle) ﴿He gave them﴾ (gave them) ﴿their Lord﴾ ﴿and their Lord protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, in coordination (*ʿaṭf*) with ﴿He gave them﴾, i.e., by their being given and their being protected. And it is said to them:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 19:

﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction﴾ (hanīʾan) is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl), meaning: enjoying it in full ease (muhannaʾīn), ﴿for what﴾ — the bāʾ here is causal (sababiyya), that is, indicating the cause.

Reclining (﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun hidden in His words ﴿upon couches arranged in rows﴾, meaning placed side by side. ﴿And We will pair them﴾ is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to "gardens", meaning We will join them ﴿with fair ones with large, lovely eyes (ḥūr ʿīn)﴾, that is, large of eye and beautiful of them.

Qur'an 52:21 — "And those who believed, and whose descendants followed them in faith, We will join their descendants with them, and We shall not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 21:

﴿Those who believed﴾ is a subject (mubtada'). ﴿And whose descendants followed them﴾ — and We made their descendants follow them; in another reading, ﴿wa-ittaba'at-hum﴾ is conjoined (ma'tuf) to ﴿āmanū﴾. ﴿Their descendants﴾ — and in another reading, ﴿dhurriyyatuhum﴾, meaning the young and the old. ﴿In faith﴾ — the adults among them, and their young children. ﴿We will join with them their descendants﴾ — the predicate (khabar) of those mentioned, in Paradise; so they will be in their rank, even if they did not perform deeds, as an honour to the fathers by gathering the children to them. ﴿And We shall not deprive them﴾ — with the lam vowelled with a fatha and with a kasra (alatnāhum) — We shall not diminish them ﴿of their deeds any﴾ — the min is superfluous (za'idah) — ﴿thing﴾, which would be added to the deeds of the children. ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾ — of deeds, good or evil — ﴿pledged﴾ (marhūn), who will be held to account for evil and recompensed for good.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 22:

﴿And We will provide them﴾ We will increase them, time after time, ﴿with fruit and meat of whatever they desire﴾ even if they do not express their request for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 23:

﴿They pass around therein﴾ (yatanazaʿūna) means they hand to one another ﴿therein﴾, i.e. in Paradise, ﴿a cup﴾ (kaʾs), i.e. of wine, ﴿wherein there is no idle talk﴾, i.e. no quarrelling or vain speech arising among them because of drinking it, ﴿nor sinfulness﴾ in it that would befall them, unlike the wine of this world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, the "Commentary of the Two Jalals") on surah 52, verse 24:

﴿And there will circulate among them﴾ for service, ﴿young boys (ghilman)﴾, slaves, ﴿for them, as if they were﴾ in beauty and delicacy, ﴿pearls well-guarded﴾, protected within the shell, because it is finer there than elsewhere.

And they will turn to one another, questioning one another (﴿وأَقْبَلَ بَعْضهمْ عَلى بَعْض يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾): one of them asks another about what they used to be upon and what they have arrived at, out of delight and acknowledgment of the blessing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 26:

﴿They say﴾, indicating the reason for their attaining (this state): ﴿Indeed, we were before this among our families﴾ in the worldly life, ﴿fearful﴾, apprehensive of the punishment of God.
﴿So God has been gracious to us﴾ with forgiveness, ﴿and has protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾, the Fire, because it enters the pores. And they also said it as an allusion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 28:

﴿Indeed, we used to call upon Him﴾ i.e., in the worldly life, ﴿nadʿūhu﴾ we worshipped Him, affirming His oneness (muwaḥḥidīn). ﴿Indeed, He﴾ with a kasra, as a resumption (istiʾnāf), though it is in meaning a causal explanation (taʿlīl); and with a fatḥa, as a causal explanation in wording (taʿlīl lafẓan). ﴿He is the Benefactor﴾ the Good-doer, the one true to His promise, ﴿the Merciful﴾ the one of great mercy.

﴿So remind﴾: Persist in reminding the polytheists, and do not turn away from it, despite their saying to you, "A soothsayer, a madman." ﴿So by the grace of your Lord﴾ by His bestowal upon you, ﴿you are not a soothsayer﴾ "بِكاهِنٍ" is the predicate (khabar) of "mā" (not), ﴿nor a madman﴾ "مَجْنُون" is conjoined to it (ma'tuf 'alayhi).
﴿Or﴾ (rather) ﴿they say﴾ ﴿he is a poet, for whom we await the vicissitudes of fate﴾, meaning the calamities of time, "so that he will perish as other poets have."

Say, "Wait" (for my destruction), "indeed I am with you among those who wait" (for your destruction). So they were punished by the sword on the Day of Badr. And *al-tarabbus* (التَّرَبُّص) means *al-intizar* (الِانْتِظار), waiting.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 52, verse 32:

﴿Do their minds command them to this?﴾ That is, their intellects, [commanding them] to their saying about him: "Sorcerer, soothsayer, madman." I.e., their minds do not command them to that. ﴿Or are they a people transgressing?﴾ That is, [rather] they are a people who transgress through their obstinacy.
﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ He fabricated the Qur'an; he did not fabricate it. ﴿Rather, they do not believe﴾ out of arrogance. So if they say, "He fabricated it":

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 34:

﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it﴾ fabricated, ﴿if they are truthful﴾ in their claim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 35:

﴿Were they created from nothing?﴾ That is, without a creator. ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ Of themselves. But it is not conceivable that a created thing exists without a creator, nor that a non-existent thing creates itself. So they must have a creator, who is Allah, the One. Why then do they not affirm His oneness and believe in His Messenger and His Book?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 36:

﴿Or were they created from nothing? Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾ No one can create them except God, the Creator; so why do they not worship Him? ﴿Rather, they are not certain﴾ of Him; for otherwise they would have believed in His Prophet.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 37:

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ — of prophethood, provision and other things — so that they might bestow them on whomever they wish, in whatever they wish. ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ — the dominant, the tyrannical. Its verb is sayṭara (to dominate), and its like is bayṭara and bayqara.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 38:

﴿Or do they have a ladder﴾ by which they ascend to the heaven, ﴿on which they listen﴾, that is, upon which they hear the speech of the angels, so that they could contend with the Prophet by their own claim, if they claim that, ﴿then let their listener﴾, the one claiming to have listened upon it, ﴿bring a clear authority﴾, a manifest and evident proof.

And this claim is similar to their claim that the angels are daughters of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 39:

﴿Or has He daughters while you have sons?﴾ according to your claim. ﴿Exalted is Allah above what you attribute to Him.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 40:

﴿Or do you ask them for a reward﴾ for what you have brought of the religion, ﴿so that they are burdened with debt﴾ (the cost of that), ﴿and so they refuse to embrace Islam﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 52, verse 41:

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down?﴾ That is, its knowledge, ﴿so that they write it down?﴾ By which they could dispute with the Prophet (ﷺ) about the resurrection and the matters of the Hereafter, according to their claim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 42:

﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ Against you, to destroy you, in the Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of the Quraysh). ﴿But those who disbelieve, they are the ones who will be ensnared.﴾ The defeated, the destroyed. So Allah protected him (ﷺ) from them, then destroyed them at Badr.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 43:

﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah? Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ [With Him] of the deities. The interrogative with "am" (or) in its places is for denunciation and reproach.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn** on Surah 52, verse 44:

﴿And if they see a piece of the sky falling﴾ (*kisfan*, meaning some part) ﴿upon them﴾, just as they said: ﴿"So drop upon us a piece of the sky"﴾ (26:187), meaning as a punishment for them, ﴿they will say﴾, "This is ﴿a heaped-up cloud﴾," piled up, "which will water us," ﴿and they will not believe﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 45:

﴿So leave them until they meet their Day, in which they will be struck senseless.﴾ They will die.

﴿The Day when﴾ is a substitute (badal, an appositive construction) for ﴿their day﴾, ﴿their scheming will avail them nothing, nor will they be helped﴾, meaning they will be prevented from the punishment in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 47:

﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong﴾ by their disbelief, ﴿there is a punishment besides that﴾ in this world, before their death, so they were punished with hunger and drought for seven years, and with killing on the Day of Badr, ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ that the punishment is coming down upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 48:

﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾ by deferring them, and let your breast not be constricted. ﴿For indeed, you are under Our eyes﴾ in full view of Us; We see you and protect you. ﴿And glorify﴾ while engaged in ﴿the praise of your Lord﴾, i.e., say: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him," ﴿when you arise﴾ from your sleep or from your gathering.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 52, verse 49:

﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾ also in reality, ﴿and at the setting of the stars﴾ (idbar, a verbal noun), i.e., after their setting, glorify Him also; or pray, in the first [part of the night] the two ʿIshāʾs (ʿishāʾayn), and in the second the Fajr; and it is said [it means] the Ṣubḥ.
